name: security-kubernetes-secret-at-rest-review
intent: Kubernetes Secret storage encryption and effective read paths
artifacts: API-server encryption config/provider order, key lifecycle, datastore snapshot policy and actual API identities.
trace: Separate base64 representation, encryption at rest and API authorization. Trace access to plaintext through datastore backups, providers and permitted API readers.
experiment: Use a local cluster/synthetic Secret and an owned storage snapshot to distinguish plaintext persistence from authorized API decryption.
disproof: Reading a Secret through an authorized API is expected even when at-rest encryption works; base64 alone is not encryption evidence.
repair: Protect storage/backups and effective read authority, verifying key rotation, rewrite and recovery behavior.
branch_decisions: API authorization, etcd encryption and node/workload delivery protect different paths. A base64 field is not encryption, while a privileged API reader obtaining plaintext may be expected. Verify encryption-provider ordering, rotation/rewrite status and storage evidence without publishing real keys; configured encryption alone does not prove historical objects were rewritten.
